mainTopic: Why the leftover פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים are left to die (ימותו) instead of being saved for next year's יום הכפורים
overview: On the previous amud, the גמרא asked why a leftover פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים must be left to die (ימותו) instead of being offered next year. The first answer is that communal offerings must come from the new year's funds, based on רבי טבי in the name of רבי יאשיה. That answer falls. It does not fit the כהן גדול's private פר, a mere גזירה seems too weak to justify death, and רב יהודה in the name of שמואל shows the 'new funds' rule is only an ideal מצוה. רבי זירא then says a גורל does not carry over from one year to the next, and a new lottery is forbidden so people won't think it does. This again explains only the שעיר, and extending it to the פר by decree is rejected. The rabbis before אביי suggest the פר is a decree because the כהן גדול might die, making it a חטאת שמתו בעליה. For the שעיר, the decree is because it would become a חטאת שעברה שנתה. The word 'decree' fits because, under רבי's 365-day year, a very young goat could still be within its first year by next יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Communal offerings must come from new funds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שעיר cannot wait until next year because communal offerings are different. It relies on רבי טבי quoting רבי יאשיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are asking about communal offerings? Communal offerings are different, as רבי טבי said in the name of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question: why not save the animal for next year? It says communal offerings follow a special rule, which it will quote in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed any animal could simply wait a year. The answer is that קרבנות ציבור have a timing rule tied to each new year's funds. So last year's animal is not right for this year.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offerings, paid for by the whole nation
You are talking about
It is different

phrases.english: You speak of communal offerings?
Communal offerings are different,
in accordance with what Rabbi Tavi said in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇרְבְּנוֹת צִבּוּר קָא אָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי קׇרְבְּנוֹת צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question (on the previous amud) of why the animals cannot be offered the following year.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing category: communal offerings follow a special rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A leftover animal could wait and be offered next יום הכפורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Communal offerings must come from the current year's funds, so last year's animal does not qualify.

steps.title: The verse: renew and bring from new funds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה learns from the פסוק 'זאת עולת חדש בחדשו' that communal offerings must come from the new תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי טבי said in the name of רבי יאשיה: the verse says, 'This is the burnt-offering of the month in its month.' The תורה is saying: renew, and bring Me an offering from the new collection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source behind the answer in step 1: a פסוק about the ראש חודש offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בחדשו' (in its renewal) is read as 'חַדֵּשׁ' — renew. Each new year's offerings should be bought with the new year's שקלים, collected in the new תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says
Renew and bring to Me
The new collection of the yearly half-שקל

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Tavi said in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya:
The verse states: 'This is the burnt-offering of the month in its month,'
the Torah said: Renew and bring Me
an offering from the new contribution.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text for the answer in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that communal offerings must come from the new year's funds
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר כח:יד, 'זאת עולת חדש בחדשו', as read by רבי יאשיה

steps.title: That works for the goat, but what about the bull?
steps.stepSummary: The 'new funds' rule explains the שעיר, which is communal. It does not explain the פר, which the כהן גדול buys with his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works well for the goat. But for the bull, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. It only covers one of the two animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 2 applies only to קרבנות ציבור. The פר of the כהן גדול is a private offering paid from his own pocket. So the rule about public funds should not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this case)
The goat (here, the communal goat of יום הכפורים)
The bull of the כהן גדול
What is there to say?

phrases.english: This works well for the goat;
for the bull, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח שָׂעִיר, פַּר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of steps 1–2 for not covering the פר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פר is a private offering, so a rule about communal funds cannot explain why it must die.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree: the bull because of the goat
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis decreed that the פר is also left to die, so that people do not confuse it with the שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: the bull because of the goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule for the פר is only rabbinic. It was made to match the rule for the שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law, the פר could be offered next year. The rabbis feared that people would then keep the שעיר too. So they extended the rule to the פר.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Because of (out of concern for)

phrases.english: It is a decree regarding the bull due to the goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the explanation against the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פר, as a private offering, should be allowed to wait for next year.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rabbinically, the פר shares the שעיר's fate to prevent confusion.

steps.title: Would the rabbis let animals die just for a decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised. Would the rabbis condemn sacred animals to die just because of a precautionary decree?
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of a decree they should be left to die?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 4. Letting an animal die is a severe result to come from a mere גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, when an offering cannot be brought, it is left to graze until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold, and the money is used. Making it die completely is a harsh loss. That seems too much for a safeguard decree.

keyTerms.meaning: They should die (be locked away until they die)

phrases.english: And due to a decree they should die?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the decree answer of step 4 as too harsh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic decree is unlikely to impose so severe a result as letting a sacred animal die.

steps.title: Second problem: the 'new funds' rule is only an ideal
steps.stepSummary: There is a further problem. רבי טבי's rule is itself only a preferred מצוה, not a requirement. So it cannot make the שעיר unusable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: this teaching of רבי טבי in the name of רבי יאשיה is itself only a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, deeper attack. This one targets the original answer from step 1 itself. It will bring proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 attacked only the decree about the פר. This step undercuts even the שעיר. If using new funds is just the ideal, then an animal bought with old funds still works. So it should not have to die.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introduces another challenge)
It itself
It is only a preferred practice, not a requirement

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מצוה' does not mean 'a commandment that must be kept'. It means 'the ideal way'. If you do it differently, the act still counts.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד: הָא דְּרַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
phrases.english: And furthermore: this statement that Rabbi Tavi said in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya
is itself only a מצוה (ideal, not essential).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: הָא דְּרַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה גּוּפַהּ מִצְוָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge, now against the base answer of steps 1–2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'new funds' rule as an explanation for the animal dying
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule that is only ideal cannot make an animal invalid, so it cannot be why the animal dies.

steps.title: שמואל: old funds still count
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל. Communal offerings of ראש חודש ניסן should come from new funds, but if they came from old funds, the obligation is still fulfilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: communal offerings brought on the first of ניסן should ideally come from the new funds. If someone brought them from the old funds, he has fulfilled his obligation. He only missed the ideal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim of step 6, that the 'new funds' rule is only an ideal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old funds can be used after the fact (בדיעבד). So the rule does not invalidate anything. The first answer therefore collapses for both the שעיר and the פר.

keyTerms.meaning: The first of ניסן, when the new year's funds begin
Old (last year's funds)
He has fulfilled the obligation
He missed the ideal way of doing it

steps.whatToRemember: The first explanation (new funds) has now fallen. It was only an ideal, so it cannot be why the animals must die.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
communal offerings that are brought on the first of Nisan —
it is a מצוה to bring them from the new funds,
and if he brought them from the old — he has fulfilled his obligation,
except that he lacked the מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the proof for the challenge in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'new funds' rule is not essential
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: if brought from old funds, יצא

steps.title: רבי זירא: a lottery does not carry over to the next year
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא gives a new reason. The animals cannot be used next year because the גורל that chose the שעיר does not last from one year to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: it is because the lottery does not set a designation from one year to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer has been rejected, so the גמרא brings a completely new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שעיר became 'לה׳' through this year's lottery. That designation expires with the year. So the animal is not valid for next year's service.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous approach)
The lottery that assigns the two goats of יום הכפורים
Establishes or fixes a designation
From one year to the next

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
because the lottery does not establish a designation
from one year to another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected 'new funds' answer with a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation replacing a rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animals die because they were not bought with new funds.
steps.terutzMaskana: They cannot be used because the lottery's designation does not carry over to the next year.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key rule about the יום הכפורים lottery: its power is limited to that year's service.

steps.title: Why not just hold a new lottery?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא. Next year, take this goat along with another one and draw lots again.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us bring it, with another goat, and draw lots again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's answer with a simple fix: hold a new lottery next year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only problem is that the old lottery expired, a fresh lottery should solve it. Then the animal would not need to die.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us bring it
And let us draw lots

phrases.english: But let us bring it and draw lots?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An expired lottery could be fixed by a new one, so death seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Decree: people might think the lottery carries over
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis forbade a new lottery. They feared people would mistakenly think the old lottery still worked from year to year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, lest people say that the lottery does set a designation from one year to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A new lottery is forbidden by a rabbinic גזירה, to protect the true rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People might see the same goat offered again and not notice the new lottery. They would then conclude the old lottery carried over. To prevent this mistake, the rabbis said the animal must die.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest people say (concern for a mistaken impression)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's approach so far: the leftover שעיר cannot be used because a lottery does not carry over to the next year, and a new lottery is forbidden so that people do not think the old one carried over. The next step challenges this approach because it does not explain the פר.

phrases.english: It is a decree lest people say
that the lottery establishes designations from one year to another.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ הַגּוֹרָל קוֹבֵעַ מִשָּׁנָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי זירא against the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree to prevent a mistaken impression
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A new lottery next year would make the goat usable.
steps.terutzMaskana: A new lottery is forbidden so people will not think the old lottery carries over.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the שעיר, רבי זירא's reason is that a lottery does not carry over between years, and re-lotting is forbidden to protect that principle. Whether this also covers the פר is challenged in the next step.

steps.title: The lottery reason does not explain the bull
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא's lottery reason works for the שעיר, but the כהן גדול's פר never had a lottery. So why can't the פר be used next year?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the goat. But for the bull, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's answer. The reason about the גורל only fits the goat, not the bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said the old animals can't be used because the גורל does not carry over to next year. But the פר of the כהן גדול is never chosen by lottery. So his reason leaves the פר unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one case)
What can be said? (what is the explanation?)
The bull (here, the כהן גדול's bull of יום כיפור)
The goat (here, the goat chosen by lottery)

phrases.english: This works out well for the goat,
phrases.notes: The goat was chosen by lottery, so רבי זירא's reason fits it.

phrases.english: but the bull — what is there to say?
phrases.notes: The bull never had a lottery.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תִּינַח שָׂעִיר, פַּר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the lottery explanation reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's explanation that the גורל does not last from year to year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The explanation covers only an animal chosen by lottery. The פר had no lottery, so the reason cannot apply to it.

steps.title: A decree on the bull because of the goat
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis extended the rule to the פר so people would not confuse it with the שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: the bull because of the goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פר is forbidden only by a rabbinic decree, as an extension of the rule for the שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פר has no lottery problem of its own. But since the פר and שעיר are both יום כיפור offerings, the rabbis treated them alike. That way nobody would come to use a leftover שעיר by comparing it to the פר.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree, a protective rule
Because of / on account of (one case due to another)

phrases.english: It is a decree — the bull on account of the goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פר needs its own reason, or else it should be allowed next year.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פר is forbidden by a decree that links it to the שעיר.

steps.title: Can a mere decree make the animals die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: is it right to put holy animals to death only because of a rabbinic decree?
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of a decree, they should die?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. A simple decree seems too weak to make the animals go to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Locking an animal away to die (ימותו) is a harsh outcome. Normally an animal that cannot be offered is left to graze until it gets a blemish. A decree based only on the פר looking like the שעיר does not seem strong enough to require death.

keyTerms.meaning: They should die (the animal is locked away until it dies)
And because of

steps.confusionAlert: ימותו here is not a punishment. It is a way of disposing of holy animals that may not be offered or redeemed. The question is whether a decree alone can send an animal to this harsher path instead of grazing.

phrases.english: And because of a decree they should die?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical challenge. A decree seems too weak a reason for such a harsh result.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the decree offered in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A protective decree should not lead to the harsh outcome of ימותו when grazing is the normal alternative.

steps.title: The rabbis before אביי: fear the כהן גדול may die
steps.stepSummary: A new reason: if the פר is kept for a year, the כהן גדול might die, and it would become a חטאת שמתו בעליה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis said before אביי: It is a decree because of a sin-offering whose owners have died.
steps.whatsHappening: The rabbis in אביי's study hall suggest a different decree for the פר. This one is tied to a type of חטאת that really does go to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פר belongs to the כהן גדול. If it waits a whole year, he might die in the meantime. Then it would become a חטאת שמתו בעליה, which by law goes to die. So the decree copies a real 'dying' category, and ימותו makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbis said it before אביי
A sin-offering whose owner died (it goes to die)
Owners of an offering

phrases.english: The rabbis said it before אביי:
It is a decree because of a sin-offering whose owners have died.
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול might die during the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם חַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new decree that answers the 'ימותו' objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason tied to a category that goes to death
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree was only about looking like the שעיר, which can't justify death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree guards against a real dying category, a חטאת שמתו בעליה.

steps.title: That works for the bull, but not the goat
steps.stepSummary: The owner-death reason fits the כהן גדול's פר, but the שעיר belongs to the whole community, and a community does not die.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the bull. But the goat — what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the earlier problem around. Now the reason fits the פר but not the שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שעיר is a communal offering, and the community never 'dies'. So the fear of a חטאת שמתו בעליה does not apply to it. The new reason leaves the goat unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offering (the שעיר is one)

phrases.english: This works out well for the bull,
but the goat — what is there to say?
phrases.notes: A communal offering has no owner who can die.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תִּינַח פַּר, שָׂעִיר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 11's challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Owner death only applies to a private offering. The communal שעיר has no owner who can die.

steps.title: A decree on the goat because of the bull
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis extended the decree to the שעיר so it would match the פר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: the goat because of the bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers again with an extension. Now the goat follows the bull's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 12, but in the opposite direction. The real reason belongs to the פר, and the שעיר is included so the two יום כיפור offerings are treated alike.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree on the goat on account of the bull

phrases.english: It is a decree — the goat on account of the bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שעיר needs its own reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שעיר is forbidden by a decree that links it to the פר.

steps.title: Again: can a decree make the goat die?
steps.stepSummary: The same objection returns. A decree that only makes the goat match the bull should not send it to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of a decree, they should die?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier objection, now against the goat's extended decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the שעיר, the death outcome rests on a decree about a decree: it is only compared to the פר. That is too weak to justify ימותו. So the גמרא needs one reason that works directly for the goat.

phrases.english: And because of a decree they should die?
phrases.notes: The same wording as step 13, now aimed at the goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 16 with the same logic used in step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A decree based only on a comparison cannot justify the harsh outcome of ימותו.

steps.title: Final reason: the sin-offering may pass its year
steps.stepSummary: Rather, the decree protects against the animal becoming a חטאת שעברה שנתה, a category that goes to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: it is a decree because of a sin-offering whose year has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier answers ('אלא') and gives a new decree. It is linked to a real category that goes to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A goat brought as a חטאת must be within its first year. If it waits until next יום כיפור, it will probably be too old and become a חטאת שעברה שנתה. That category itself goes to die, so ימותו now fits the goat directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer for a new one)
A sin-offering animal that is past its first year (it goes to die)

phrases.english: Rather: it is a decree because of
a sin-offering whose year has passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם חַטָּאת שֶׁעִבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the decree 'שעיר אטו פר' (step 16) with a new decree that applies directly to the goat. The 'חטאת שמתו בעליה' reason of step 14 still stands for the פר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason tied to a dying category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree only linked one animal to the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree guards against a real dying category, a חטאת שעברה שנתה.

steps.title: Why call it a decree? It is truly too old!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders: by next יום כיפור the goat will surely be over a year old. So it is fully disqualified, not just by decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: A decree? It is itself a sin-offering whose year has passed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording 'decree'. It seems the goat is truly too old by תורה law, so no decree should be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full year will pass between one יום כיפור and the next. So the goat should certainly be over a year old. That makes it a real חטאת שעברה שנתה, so why call the rule only a 'decree'?

keyTerms.meaning: It itself

phrases.english: A decree?

phrases.aramaic: הִיא גּוּפַהּ חַטָּאת שֶׁעִבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ הִיא!
phrases.english: It is itself a sin-offering whose year has passed!

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה הִיא גּוּפַהּ חַטָּאת שֶׁעִבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 18 is described.
steps.kashyaTarget: Calling the 'חטאת שעברה שנתה' rule a decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the goat is certainly too old by next year, it is disqualified by law itself. Calling it a 'decree' makes no sense.

steps.title: Not difficult: this follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי, a very young goat might still be under a year old next יום כיפור. So the ban is only a decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult — it follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the goat is not always too old. It depends on how a 'year' is counted, following רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי counts a year as 365 days. The Jewish calendar year is about 354 days, so it runs about 11 days short. A goat that was only a few days old this יום כיפור could still be under 365 days next יום כיפור, as long as the year was not a leap year. So it is not always disqualified by law, and banning all such goats is a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
According to רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

phrases.english: This is not difficult — in accordance with רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 and sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case through a tannaitic opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every goat is surely over a year old by the next יום כיפור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי's 365-day year, a very young goat may still qualify. So the general ban is a decree.

steps.title: The ברייתא: how to count a full year
steps.stepSummary: The source for רבי: 'שנה תמימה' means 365 solar days. The חכמים say it means twelve months from date to date.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'A full year' — he counts 365 days, like the number of days in the solar year. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: he counts twelve months from day to day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows רבי's way of counting a year. It backs up the answer in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'שנה תמימה' is about selling a house in a walled city. רבי reads it as 365 days, a solar year. The חכמים read it as twelve months from date to date, about 354 days. Only under רבי's count can a young goat still be under a year old next יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
A full year (Vayikra 25:30, about houses in a walled city)
Days of the solar year
From day to day (the same calendar date)

steps.whatToRemember: Each animal is sent to die by a decree tied to a real dying category. The פר is covered by the concern of a חטאת שמתו בעליה (the כהן גדול might die). The שעיר is covered by the concern of a חטאת שעברה שנתה. The word 'decree' fits the goat because, under רבי's 365-day year, a very young goat could still be within its year next יום כיפור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא pins down why a rule is only rabbinic. The answer comes from a basic dispute about how to count a year, borrowed from the laws of houses in walled cities.
